C.4 Dimension induction and deficient ranks

First prove, for every d,t≥0d,t\geq 0 with 2​t≤d2t\leq d, the full-rank statement: for every η>0\eta>0, some selection has full span, budget max⁡{1,2​d−t}\max\{1,2d-t\}, and risk at most (1+t/d)​LD⋆+η(1+t/d)L_{D}^{\star}+\eta. At d=t=0d=t=0 use one sample; all features and the minimum-norm solution are zero. The convention for this auxiliary case is t/d=0t/d=0. Proceed by strong induction on dd.

If any nonzero feature has zero gradient, use it as a singleton anchor. The projected parameters are (d−1,(t−1)+)(d-1,(t-1)_{+}), where (t−1)+=max⁡{t−1,0}(t-1)_{+}=\max\{t-1,0\}. They satisfy the induction condition and

1+max⁡{1,2​(d−1)−(t−1)+}≤max⁡{1,2​d−t},(t−1)+d−1≤td.1+\max\{1,2(d-1)-(t-1)_{+}\}\leq\max\{1,2d-t\},\qquad\frac{(t-1)_{+}}{d-1}\leq\frac{t}{d}.

For d=1d=1, necessarily t=0t=0; the quotient is the already settled zero-dimensional case and the total budget is two. Use tolerance η/2\eta/2 in the projected problem and η/2\eta/2 in the lifting lemma.

Otherwise apply Lemma 23. An exact certificate within budget gives the claim immediately. A 2​d2d-row minimum certificate is handled by (C.2). In the remaining case, the anchor has dimension 2≤a≤t2\leq a\leq t and a+1a+1 rows. Set

d′=d−a,t′=t−a+1.d^{\prime}=d-a,\qquad t^{\prime}=t-a+1.

Then d′<dd^{\prime}<d, 1≤t′<t1\leq t^{\prime}<t, 2​t′≤d′2t^{\prime}\leq d^{\prime}, and

(a+1)+(2​d′−t′)=2​d−t,t′d′≤td.(a+1)+(2d^{\prime}-t^{\prime})=2d-t,\qquad\frac{t^{\prime}}{d^{\prime}}\leq\frac{t}{d}.

For the latter inequality, cross multiplication reduces to d⁡(a−1)≥t​ad(a-1)\geq ta, which follows from d≥2​td\geq 2t and a≥2a\geq 2. Apply the induction hypothesis on the complete projected dataset and lift, again dividing the tolerance equally. The auxiliary case t=0t=0 closes as well: without a singleton anchor, a minimum active certificate has at most 2​d2d rows and is exact within budget.

Now let the actual feature rank be m≤dm\leq d and put n=2​d−tn=2d-t. Rank zero is exact with one selected row. For m>0m>0, identify the feature span with ℝm\mathbb{R}^{m} and set k=(2​m−n)+k=(2m-n)_{+}. Direct integer arithmetic gives

2​k≤m,max⁡{1,2​m−k}≤n,km≤td.2k\leq m,\qquad\max\{1,2m-k\}\leq n,\qquad\frac{k}{m}\leq\frac{t}{d}.

The full-rank result in dimension mm therefore proves the same bound. For completeness, the minimum-norm solution belongs to the feature span: its orthogonal projection has identical predictions and smaller norm unless the orthogonal component is zero. The selected span equals the full feature span, so the same argument applies after selection. This justifies both coordinate reduction and return to the original minimum-norm convention. We have proved the additive bound for every η>0\eta>0; take η=ε​LD⋆\eta=\varepsilon L_{D}^{\star} to obtain the upper bound in Theorem 1.

C.5 Matching lower bound, including omitted coordinates

Take the uniform 2​d2d-row dataset (ej,1),(ej,3)(e_{j},1),(e_{j},3), j∈[d]j\in[d]. Its full solution is (2,…,2)(2,\ldots,2) and LD⋆=1L_{D}^{\star}=1. Every output uu has

LD​(u)=1+1d​∑j=1d(uj−2)2.L_{D}(u)=1+\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d}(u_{j}-2)^{2}.

If a coordinate retains two, one, or zero rows, its least possible squared displacement is respectively 00, 11, or 44. In the last case the minimum-norm rule forces uj=0u_{j}=0. If AA coordinates retain one row and BB retain none, the budget gives A+2​B≥tA+2B\geq t and hence LD​(u)≥1+(A+4​B)/d≥1+t/dL_{D}(u)\geq 1+(A+4B)/d\geq 1+t/d. Retain one endpoint on exactly tt coordinates and both endpoints on the others. Equal weights within each retained pair, followed by normalization of all weights, attain 1+t/d1+t/d. This proves the matching sharpness and completes the theorem.

C.6 Formal theorem and dependency map

The supplied project uses Lean 4.19.0 and mathlib commit c44e0c8ee63ca166450922a373c7409c5d26b00b. Its declaration

UpperHalf.certifiedUpperHalfLaw : UpperHalf.SharpUpperHalfLaw

combines a universal, arbitrary-rank, normalized-selection upper bound with a concrete dataset attaining the matching lower bound. Its definitions include the evaluation risk, support size, selected feature span, and both minimization requirements in the minimum-norm learner. The equality for Γd\Gamma_{d} follows from these two dataset-level statements and (2).

Lean module Mathematical role
NontrivialAnchor Direct positive-basis simplex-anchor proof
MaximalRegression Independent-line structure for the complete dataset
LineCompression Legal 2​d−t2d-t-row selection and sharp line-risk bound
AnchorLift, CoordinateAnchor Actual weighted regression limit from the projected instance
IntrinsicReduction Deficient-rank coordinates and the minimum-norm rule
FullRankInduction Closed dimension induction, including the zero-gap case
Sharpness, Certified Attaining lower bound and the complete original-data theorem

Run setup.ps1 from the formal project, or, with dependencies installed, run lake build and lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true FullTheoremCheck.lean. The complete theorem’s axiom audit returns only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The formalization covers Theorem 1; the supplied symbolic checks for Theorem 2 are documented separately in Appendix E.

Appendix D The block frontier and the matrix formulation

D.1 A basis facet for one block

Consider a+1a+1 rows spanning ℝa\mathbb{R}^{a}, with positive evaluation weights, positive optimal loss, and every aa rows independent. Scale by the square roots of the weights, whiten the Hessian, and normalize the residual to obtain B⊤​B=IaB^{\top}B=I_{a}, B⊤​e=0B^{\top}e=0, and ‖e‖=1\|e\|=1. Since BB has a+1a+1 rows, B​B⊤=I−e​e⊤BB^{\top}=I-ee^{\top}. Write bi⊤b_{i}^{\top} for its rows. Choose ii maximizing ei2e_{i}^{2}, so ei2≥1/(a+1)>0e_{i}^{2}\geq 1/(a+1)>0. Deleting row ii gives normal matrix I−bi​bi⊤I-b_{i}b_{i}^{\top} and displacement of squared norm

ei2​‖bi‖2(1−‖bi‖2)2=1−ei2ei2≤a.\frac{e_{i}^{2}\|b_{i}\|^{2}}{(1-\|b_{i}\|^{2})^{2}}=\frac{1-e_{i}^{2}}{e_{i}^{2}}\leq a.

Here Sherman–Morrison applies because 1−‖bi‖2=ei2>01-\|b_{i}\|^{2}=e_{i}^{2}>0. Thus a basis facet has risk at most (a+1)(a+1) times the block optimum. Its unique interpolant is independent of the positive training weights. For zero optimal loss, any basis facet is exact.

min⁡∑j∉JJ⊆[k]|J|=s⁡aj​ℓj(s<k).\min_{\begin{subarray}{c}J\subseteq[k]\\ |J|=s\end{subarray}}\sum_{j\notin J}a_{j}\ell_{j}\quad(s<k). (D.1)

For a fixed partition define

Ψs​(a)=maxℓ∈Δk⁡min⁡∑j∉J|J|=s⁡aj​ℓj.\Psi_{s}(a)=\max_{\ell\in\Delta_{k}}\min_{|J|=s}\sum_{j\notin J}a_{j}\ell_{j}.

The translated construction attains the same worst-case value in the supremum: approximate any zero maximizing masses by positive masses.

Finally, an active subset RR uses at most dd dimensions. Distributing all remaining dimensions among its blocks decreases their reciprocal sum and increases its candidate value. Appendix E Exact verification and proof index

E.1 Reproduction and scope

The anonymous source package includes verification/verify_exact.py. With Python 3.12 and SymPy 1.13.2, run the following from the package root:

python -m pip install -r verification/requirements.txt
python verification/verify_exact.py

The script uses exact rational arithmetic and symbolic identities. It writes verification/exact_check_results.json, including the hashes of the script and the five-dimensional proof source. It requires no dataset, network connection after installation, or access to a prior draft. The reported checks cover algebraic identities, selected symbolic ranks, a finite rational grid for one boundary-rank diagnostic, all nonempty supports of size at most six in the seven-point example, and the explicit path/cycle/star probability constructions. The script is not a formal proof assistant and does not test all root configurations.

The lower-bound support check exhausts all 126 nonempty supports: 19 have full rank and 107 have deficient rank. On the full-rank supports it checks the block counts used in the analytic argument; on every deficient support it computes the minimum evaluation-norm squared distance from the translation vector to the selected span. The smallest such distance is five. It also solves the stated attaining full-rank selection and obtains the ratio 11/511/5 exactly. The analytic interpolation argument in Appendix B.7, rather than a finite sample of training weights, covers arbitrary positive weights on each full-rank support.

E.2 Algebra-to-proof mapping

The diagnostic identifiers are stable local equation identifiers used by the checker. Their correspondence with the paper is as follows.

Checker identifiers Mathematical object in this paper
9.1 Same-type crossing relation, (B.8)
9.2 Same-index mixed relation, (B.9)
9.3 Cross-index positive representation, (B.10)
9.4 Type-C/type-A cross relation, (B.11)
9.5 Shared-index circuit relation, (B.12)
12.2–12.8 Block-restriction representations following (B.14)
13.1–13.3 Remaining type-C relations, (B.15)–(B.17)
Support checks Seven-point construction, Appendix B.7
Graph checks Explicit probabilities in Lemma 21

Generic symbolic rank calculations do not by themselves establish rank at every positive specialization. The paper gives the structural rank and positivity arguments; the finite boundary-rank grid is explicitly diagnostic. Likewise, the graph checks evaluate the listed probabilities but do not replace the circuit-plane intersection lemmas or the transfer from graph probabilities to actual regression risk.

E.3 Dependency index

For the upper bound, Appendix B.1 establishes the training interface and comparison moment; Appendix B.2 proves the active-space and polar-slice restrictions; Appendix B.3 closes the shared-root rank-three case; Appendix B.4 treats the rank-two plane graph; Appendix B.5 closes the other rank-three case; and Appendix B.6 handles all regression degeneracies. The only lower-dimensional interior input is the five-point upper bound in four dimensions from Zhang (2026, Theorem 47). The dimension-three boundary input is proved in Appendix A. The exact lower bound is in Appendix B.7.
